scenario.fault_family: routing daemon down (ABR isolates an area)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a change on r7, routes for 17.x.x.x (R7 loopbacks),
67.0.0.0/8 (R7-R6 link), and 70.0.0.0/8 (R7 LAN) disappeared
from r1's routing table. R7 used to have an OSPF adjacency
with R6. Identify what's wrong.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r7 ospfd daemon
Mechanism: r7 owns the 17.1.{1..4}.0/24 loopback range, the
  70.0.0.0/8 LAN, and forms the only OSPF adjacency with r6
  over 67.0.0.0/8. With its ospfd dead, r6 ages out r7's
  prefixes and they propagate as withdrawals through area 1
  and the backbone. r1 loses visibility into the r7 region.
Localization: r7
Root cause: ospfd not running on r7
Fix: `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on r7

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r7" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.

agent.diagnosis_text: The ospfd process on r7 crashed and exited approximately 2 minutes after lab startup. The FRR log on r7 shows the sequence clearly: ospfd started and read its configuration at 13:56:42, successfully completed a Database Description exchange with r6 (router-ID 16.1.4.1) at 13:57:29, then abruptly shut down at 13:58:14 with the message "Client 'ospf' (session id 0) encountered an error and is shutting down." Zebra immediately de-installed the 64 OSPF routes ospfd had installed, including r7's loopbacks (17.1.x.0/24), its LAN (70.0.0.0/8), and the R6–R7 link (67.0.0.0/8). Since ospfd is no longer running, r7 originates no LSAs, r6's eth2 (67.1.1.1/8) has zero OSPF neighbors, and the rest of the domain — including r1 — never receives r7's prefixes. The on-disk `/etc/frr/frr.conf` is completely intact with the correct `router ospf` block and all six `network` statements, and `/etc/frr/daemons` correctly sets `ospfd=yes`, so no configuration file needs to be changed. The root cause is that ospfd on r7 terminated abnormally after forming its adjacency, leaving the daemon absent while the config is healthy. The corrective fix is to restart FRR on r7 (`service frr restart` or `systemctl restart frr`), which will re-launch ospfd, load the existing frr.conf, re-establish the Full adjacency with r6, and re-flood r7's LSAs so that r1 and all other OSPF speakers re-learn the 17.x.x.x, 67.0.0.0/8, and 70.0.0.0/8 prefixes.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies r7 as the affected device (ospfd on r7 crashed/terminated and needs restart).
The report explicitly identifies the ospfd daemon/OSPF as the failed component, describing its crash, absence, and impact on LSAs and adjacency.
The diagnosis states ospfd terminated, zebra immediately removed the OSPF routes and the adjacency dropped, which explains why r7's prefixes were withdrawn and propagated through the domain.
Recommends restarting the FRR service on r7 to relaunch ospfd and restore LSAs, which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log contains concrete command outputs (ps, show ip ospf neighbor, cat frr.conf, daemons, and frr.log) demonstrating ospfd terminated on r7 while config on disk is intact; the agent's inferences (route withdrawals, neighbor loss, restart FRR fix) follow logically and address the key alternatives. Evidence, causality, and necessary checks are all present.
